initialCorrections: Windows FFmpeg declares Vorbis startup CodecDelay 2666667 ns (128 samples), while Linux FFmpeg omits it. The bounded Vorbis profile now permits whole-sample floor/ceil delay up to the largest half-window, preserving the original header. First MSVC native exit 1 and Qt CTest exit 8 are retained.

Windows FFmpeg stores an audible-remainder BlockDuration plus DiscardPadding on the final Vorbis packet. Packet/window mode duration is now authoritative and padding is subtracted once. Native exit 1 and Qt exit 8 from the second attempt are retained; tests exercise both duration conventions and exact sample lengths.
A private pre-fix Linux UI run and preliminary sanitizer run were stopped for the source correction. The Linux UI process exit 143 is retained. Final binaries were rebuilt before full verification.
Legacy coarse timestamp scales keep the prior Vorbis BlockDuration tolerance; shared WebM remains limited to 1 ms ticks.
limitations: Exactly two required scalar VP8/VP9/AV1 plus Opus/Vorbis views of one WebM resource, known-duration zero-offset VOD and complete finite Clusters. Vorbis mono/stereo 48 kHz, bounded setup/floor 1 and no metadata SeekPreRoll.
Layout/index snapshots are copied; worst-case memory, maximum index size and multi-hour throughput have not been stress-tested.
Container/header validation is not full elementary-stream entropy validation; actual decoder output remains authoritative.
Native decoded hashes and timestamp comparison do not measure physical output synchronization.
Installed Windows EXEs/INIs were not replaced.
